turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Feels apprehensive or unsure when facing an unfamiliar or risky situation
turning_points.what_changes: At scene3_beat1 Krista is merely 'unsure' about a dark trail -- a vague, low-stakes apprehension. Here she cries out in real alarm ('Beth!') immediately after hearing a terrifying scream, reacting to an actual crisis rather than an imagined worry -- a clear jump in intensity and stakes.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Feels apprehensive or unsure when facing an unfamiliar or risky situation
turning_points.what_changes: Moments after crying out to Beth, Krista is found alone at the foundation 'full of fear and confusion' -- the same unbroken fear event continuing forward, not a new separate escalation.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Feels apprehensive or unsure when facing an unfamiliar or risky situation
turning_points.what_changes: The fear-and-confusion state from the woods carries through, unbroken, into the aftermath at the house with police present, now surfacing as audible sobbing -- the same continuous emotional arc, not a fresh trigger.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Feels apprehensive or unsure when facing an unfamiliar or risky situation
turning_points.what_changes: Directly continuing the sobbing scene, Krista now puts the trauma into words ('we heard her screaming... found her horse') -- the same unbroken emotional beat, now given verbal form rather than a new turning point.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Approaches her hobbyhorse 'Bella' with gentle, nurturing care, treating the imaginative play as emotionally real
turning_points.what_changes: Krista is shown carrying the same hobbyhorse into a real competition arena, a concrete callback to the hobbyhorse-comforting introduced at scene3_beat1 -- despite the trauma of losing Holly, the same specific object and activity persists, showing this part of her identity survives intact rather than being erased.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Compliant -- goes along with the group's decisions, especially Beth's, without objection
turning_points.what_changes: At scene6_beat4 Krista simply trots off after Beth without pushback -- pure passive deference. Here, when Beth deflects John's questions, Krista actively volunteers new information ('A friend,' 'She wouldn't tell us,' 'El Vaquero') against the grain of Beth's visible reluctance, risking friction with her friend to help find Holly -- a real escalation from physical following to independent moral action at social cost.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows genuine concern and empathy specifically for Holly
turning_points.what_changes: Krista's closing line, 'Holly was always nice to me. I really hope you find her,' directly answers her earlier worried call of 'Holly?' in the woods -- the same specific concern for Holly, now given full, explicit voice months later, confirming it was never a passing reaction but an enduring, concrete attachment.
